key_insight: Routing-aware pruning removes two-qubit gates only when their expected fidelity gain outweighs the hardware cost of executing them, making circuit simplification compatible with both NISQ and fault-tolerant quantum systems.
engineering_relevance: This offers a unified compilation lever to cut routing overhead, reduce gate counts, and improve output fidelity across different quantum hardware stacks.
method: Evaluate each parametric two-qubit gate against an architecture-independent fidelity-loss bound for omitting it.
Compare that bound with a hardware-specific routing execution cost model for NISQ and FTQC settings.
Derive an analytical pruning boundary using rotation angle, qubit distance, and noise parameters.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks show up to 48.6% gate-count reduction and up to 47.7% fidelity improvement in NISQ simulations, with FT hardware analysis indicating the approach remains useful across code distances and physical error rates.
watch_item: Pruning decisions depend on accurate hardware noise and routing-cost models, so mismatch between the model and deployed hardware could reduce expected gains.
paper_title: Quantum Circuit Pruning: From NISQ Architectures to Fault-Tolerant Operations
